---
title: "Migrating from v0.3"
---

Version 0.4 moves every module of the package to a new layered layout. It is a
clean break: the old import paths do not work, and there are no compatibility
aliases. This page lists where each v0.3 name went.

Zenodo keeps the earlier versions: v0.3 at
[doi:10.5281/zenodo.22663087](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22663087) and v0.2 at
[doi:10.5281/zenodo.22162871](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22162871).
Licence history: in v0.3 and earlier, the EELS physics followed abTEM
(GPL-3.0), the multislice base physics followed py_multislice (which has no
licence), and the centre-of-mass fit chain (`fit_2D`, `fit_origin`, the
centre-of-mass measurement), the scan-rotation search, the bright-field shift
estimators and the SSB Warp kernels followed py4DSTEM (GPL-3.0). Those
archives carry an Apache-2.0 label, but these parts of them are not
Apache-2.0 code. v0.4 replaces all of them with clean-room rewrites. v0.3 and
earlier also held code from torchvision (BSD-3-Clause) and quantem (MIT)
without their notices. v0.4 carries both notices.

The layers, from the bottom up:

| Package | Holds |
|---|---|
| `scatterem.utils`, `scatterem.crystal`, `scatterem.rotation` | general helpers, crystallography, rotations |
| `scatterem.physics` | constants, optics, structures, potentials, transmission functions, propagation |
| `scatterem.data` | the 4D-STEM containers, metadata, calibration, the paper datasets |
| `scatterem.nn` | differentiable operators: the ptychography kernels, the PRISM and multislice scan operators |
| `scatterem.simulation` | forward simulation: PRISM-EELS and its driver |
| `scatterem.reconstruction` | the FF-STEM reconstructions and `run` |
| `scatterem.vis` | plotting |

## The five changes most code needs

1. Rename `Dataset4dstem` to `Dataset4DStem`. The same applies to
   `DatasetVirtualBrightField4dstem` and `PublicDataset4dstem`.
2. Replace the dataset methods with `run(dataset, config)`. See
   [The reconstruction methods](#the-reconstruction-methods).
3. Import the paper datasets from `scatterem.data.public`, not
   `scatterem.datasets`. `from scatterem import You2026Carbon` still works.
4. Use the new multislice substrate in `scatterem.physics`: `AtomSet` from
   `scatterem.physics.atom_set`, `potential_stack` from
   `scatterem.physics.potential_stack`, `thin_slice_transmission` from
   `scatterem.physics.thin_slice`, `debroglie_at` (the electron wavelength)
   from `scatterem.physics.constants`, `lens_wavefront` (the aberration
   function) from `scatterem.physics.optics`. The names, arguments and
   defaults are new;
   see [The physics base layer](#the-physics-base-layer).
   `scatterem.simulation` re-exports nothing.
5. Replace `StemEelsSimulator` with `PrismEelsSimulator`. See
   [The STEM-EELS driver](#the-stem-eels-driver).

## The reconstruction methods

The `Dataset4dstem` methods that ran a reconstruction are gone. Each one is now a
configuration object that you pass to `scatterem.reconstruction.run`. `run`
returns a result and does not change the dataset.

| v0.3 | v0.4 |
|---|---|
| `dataset.determine_aberrations_(correct_order=2)` | `dataset.meta = run(dataset, AberrationFitConfig(correct_order=2, bright_field_mask_threshold=t)).applied_to(dataset.meta)` |
| `dataset.direct_ptychography(upsample=2.0)` | `run(dataset, DirectPtychographyConfig(upsample=2.0, bright_field_mask_threshold=t)).phase` |
| `dataset.tilt_corrected_dark_field(upsample=2.0)` | `run(dataset, TiltCorrectedDarkFieldConfig(upsample=2.0, bright_field_mask_threshold=t)).image` |
| `dataset.fused_full_field(upsample=2.0)` | `run(dataset, FusedFullFieldConfig(upsample=2.0, n_dark_field_segments=32)).fused` |
| `correction_method="autofocus"` with C10, C12a and C12b of `meta.aberrations` zero (other slots, such as Cs, may be set), `meta.defocus_guess` 0 and a failed bright-field-shift fit: the autofocus searched around zero, with no error | the same call raises `ValueError`; set a start, for example `dataset.meta.aberrations.array[0] = -50.0` |

Here `t = dataset.bright_field_mask_threshold`. `AberrationFitConfig` and
`DirectPtychographyConfig` are in `scatterem.reconstruction.ptychography.direct`,
`TiltCorrectedDarkFieldConfig` in `scatterem.reconstruction.darkfield`, and
`FusedFullFieldConfig` in `scatterem.reconstruction.fusion.ffstem`. The
default bright-field mask threshold is 0.5 in `AberrationFitConfig` and
`DirectPtychographyConfig`, and 0.3 in `TiltCorrectedDarkFieldConfig`. In
`FusedFullFieldConfig` the default is `None`, which uses the threshold of the
dataset. The paper path uses the threshold of the dataset, so pass it
explicitly to the other three. `result.as_tuple()` gives
the tuple that the function form returns.

The functions `direct_ptychography`, `tilt_corrected_dark_field` and
`fused_full_field` are still importable from `scatterem` and
`scatterem.reconstruction`.

## The STEM-EELS driver

`StemEelsSimulator` and `StemEelsResult` are removed. `PrismEelsSimulator` and
`PrismResult` in `scatterem.simulation.eels` replace them. The new driver takes
the edge and the energy per call, not in the constructor, and it has one method
per output.

| v0.3 | v0.4 |
|---|---|
| `StemEelsSimulator(structure, edge=e, epsilon=x, prism=True, ...)` then `.simulate()` | `PrismEelsSimulator(structure, ...)` then `.eels_cube(e, epsilon=x)`; `structure` is an `AtomSet` |
| `StemEelsSimulator(..., prism=False).simulate()` (conventional multislice) | `multislice_transition_potential(...)` with the inputs from the driver; see [Checking your setup](eels.qmd#checking-your-setup) |
| `prism_eels_image(...)` built by hand | `PrismEelsSimulator.eels_map(e, detector_mrad=..., ...)` or `.qeels(...)` |
| `simulate_window((lo, hi), n_energies=n)` | a loop over `epsilon` and `torch.trapezoid`; see [Simulate STEM-EELS](eels.qmd#an-energy-window-and-several-edges) |
| `simulate_edges([e1, e2])` | one driver call per edge |
| `backend="auto"`, `xc=`, `order=`, `potential_scale=` (constructor) | `transitions=dict(wavefunctions="auto", xc=..., order=..., potential_scale=...)` (per call) |
| `result.cube` | `result.data` |
| `transition_potential_multislice(...)` | `multislice_transition_potential(...)`: renamed to match `prism_transition_potential`; the arguments and the results are the same |
| `result.sampling` | `result.detector_sampling` |
| `result.energy_losses`, `result.edge`, `result.epsilon` | unchanged |
| — | `PrismEelsSimulator.elastic_cbed()`: elastic 4D-STEM by PRISM, new |

Three differences change numbers:

- The driver builds the specimen with the new physics base layer:
  `potential_stack` with its defaults (Hann rolloff 1/3, band-limited point
  values, `edge_snap=True`) and `thin_slice_transmission` with the band limit
  2/3 of v0.3. Elastic and EELS results change: in the BiP-PRISM
  map-scaling study the new transmissions alone change the map shapes by
  7-8 %. With
  `displacements=True`, a given `seed` gives other thermal draws than in v0.3.
  See [The physics base layer](#the-physics-base-layer).
- The driver probe uses `scatterem.physics.optics.smooth_disc` with a
  logistic rim of 1 pixel (`rim_px=1.0`), the rim of the PRISM beam set. The
  v0.3 driver used a hard disk. Values near the aperture edge
  change. In partitioned BiP-PRISM maps the probe alone changes the map shape
  by up to 6 %, in exact PRISM maps by less than 1 %.
- The transition potentials are new. `build_transition_potentials` and the
  radial states are rewritten from the first-Born physics, so every EELS
  intensity changes:
  - The transition potentials have an absolute first-Born scale (Å²/eV). With
    GPAW states at 200 kV, the amplitude of the dipole channels is about 7.3e-4
    (K edges) and 4.3e-4 (L23 edges) of the v0.3 value. The ratio depends on
    the beam energy through the $1/v^2$ factor and the flux factor: at 300 kV
    it is 6.4e-4 to 6.6e-4 (K), 3.7e-4 to 3.9e-4 (L23) and 2.9e-4 to 3.0e-4
    (La M45), and at 100 kV 9.2e-4 (O K) and 5.2e-4 to 5.5e-4 (L23). So no
    single factor converts v0.3 values to v0.4 values.
  - Channels with $l' = l$ use a continuum that is orthogonalised to the bound
    orbital. This removes a spurious monopole term.
  - `free_continuum_wavefunction` is normalised per Rydberg: it carries the
    factor $(\pi k)^{-1/2}$.
  - The GPAW atom uses a denser radial grid, so the GPAW states and core
    energies change slightly. The core energies of the 11 edges we tested
    move by 0.0002-0.18 eV (largest: Fe L1 +0.18 eV, Al K +0.15 eV).

  With GPAW states, after a best scalar fit, the map shapes change by
  0.03-0.6 % for the K, L23 and M45 edges we tested and by 1.4 % for Fe L1
  (300 kV). With hydrogenic states, they change by 18-61 %. The forward model does
  not change: given the same transition potentials, the kernels give the v0.3
  maps. See [The BiP-PRISM paper and v0.4](eels.qmd#bip-prism-paper-v04).

The EELS code also follows these rules in v0.4:

- Each ionized site has the weight of its atom in the elastic potential:
  `site_fraction` when the structure has a partial occupancy, else 1. A site
  with fraction 0 does not ionize. `PrismEelsSimulator` makes one kernel call
  for each different nonzero fraction.
- With `displacements=True`, one thermal draw moves the elastic atoms and the
  ionized atoms of a configuration by the same offsets.
- `prism_eels_image`, `prism_transition_potential`,
  `prism_transition_potential_hybrid` and `multislice_transition_potential`
  put each site in the slice that
  `BeamPartition.uniform(nz).bin_index` gives (the slice rule of
  `potential_stack`), not in `floor(z % 1 * nz)`. A site just before a slice
  edge can go to the next slice.
- `build_transition_potentials(..., method="auto", device="cpu")` builds on the
  CPU. With `device=None`, the build goes to CUDA when CUDA is present.

Two defaults stay as in v0.3:

- The wavefunctions default is `wavefunctions="auto"` (v0.3: `backend="auto"`).
  It uses GPAW when it is installed. Without GPAW, it falls back to hydrogenic
  states, as v0.3 did, and now also emits a `HydrogenicFallbackWarning`.
  Install `scatterem[eels]` for quantitative results. The choice of states
  stays the same, but the numbers change with the new transition potentials
  (see above).
- `prism_eels_image` keeps the v0.3 defaults (`mag_preserve=True`,
  `focal_backprop=None`, detector de-chirp on). Its `contract` default is now
  `"auto"`, which picks the cheaper of `"columns"` and `"probe"` for each atom.
  Both orders compute the same result to rounding (relative tolerance 1e-11 in
  float64). Pass `contract="columns"` to force the v0.3 order.

## The physics base layer

v0.4 replaces the physics base layer with new code that has a new API. v0.3
and earlier based this layer on py_multislice: the frequency grids, the band
limits, the scattering factors, the structure container, the potential builder
and the transmission function. Two teams wrote the new modules. A
specification team that knew the former code wrote a behavioural contract,
and a separate team wrote the code from that contract and the published
literature. `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` describes the process and its limits. No
name, argument name, unit string, default or argument order of the former code
is kept, except the NumPy and PyTorch convention names `shape`, `dtype` and
`device` and the generic names `msd`, `depth` and `jitter`. The numbers
change. The projected potentials differ from v0.3 by 0.8-9 % (relative L2),
and by up to 15 % on very coarse grids; the new ones are closer to the exact
Fourier sum (1e-4 to 6e-4 against 2-11 % for v0.3). In the BiP-PRISM
map-scaling study the new transmissions change the EELS map shapes by 7-8 %.
Item 8 of "Numbers that move" in the v0.4.0 release notes gives all the
measurements.

The tables list every change. "Removed" means that no direct replacement
exists; the last column says what to do. A "Former name" can be a name of
the development code between v0.3 and v0.4 that no public release had, for
example `physics.grid.*`, `physics.scattering.*`, `_potential_common.*`,
`AVOGADRO_CONSTANT`, `circular_aperture` and `interaction_parameter`. The
table [Every v0.3 public name](#every-v0.3-public-name) lists the names of
the v0.3 release.

### Frequency grids and band limits (`scatterem.physics.periodic_sampling`)

| Former name | v0.4 name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `physics.grid.fft_frequencies(shape, extent, meshed=True)` | `dft_sample_frequencies(PeriodicGrid(points, lengths))` | returns one broadcastable float64 array per axis; call `numpy.broadcast_arrays` for full grids |
| `physics.grid.mesh_axes(axes)` | removed | use `numpy.broadcast_arrays` |
| `physics.grid.fft_frequency_grid` | `scatterem.physics._frequency_grid.fft_frequency_grid` | no public re-export; the torch twin of `dft_sample_frequencies` |
| `physics.grid.band_limit_mask(shape, limit, soft, rfft, dtype, device, taper=None)` | `ellipse_mask(shape, nyquist_fraction, *, half_last_axis, fade_depth=0.0, device=None, dtype=None)` | `shape` is always the full grid shape; the smooth edge is a Hann edge of depth `fade_depth` inside the cut, not an erf edge |
| `physics.grid.band_limit(array, limit=2/3, qspace_in=True, qspace_out=True, soft=None, rfft=False, taper=None)` | `lowpass_ellipse(field, nyquist_fraction, *, fade_depth=0.0)` | real space in and out; no default fraction; for a spectrum, multiply by `ellipse_mask` |
| `physics.grid.antialias_aperture(shape, sampling, cutoff=0.6666666, dtype, device)` | `CircularPassBand(PeriodicGrid.from_pixel_sizes(shape, sampling), cut_fraction, rim_samples=2.0).mask(device=None, dtype=None)` | the rim width is `rim_samples` frequency steps of the coarser axis, not a fixed width in 1/Å |
| `physics.grid.antialias_limit`, `antialias_taper_fraction` | removed | read `CircularPassBand.cut_radius`, `.rim_width` and `.flat_radius` [1/Å] |
| `physics.grid.antialias_cutoff_gpts(shape, sampling, cutoff)` | `CircularPassBand.min_crop_shape()` | the box is `2 J + 1` samples per axis; it does not keep the parity of the grid |
| `physics.grid.bandlimit_waves(waves, aperture)` | `apply_pass_band(field, mask)` | |
| `physics.grid.ANTIALIAS_CUTOFF`, `ANTIALIAS_TAPER` | removed | give the cut fraction each time; 2/3 is the conventional value |
| — | `mask_cache_stats()`, `clear_mask_cache()` | new: the masks are kept in a bounded cache |

### Scattering amplitudes (`scatterem.physics.atom_amplitudes`)

| Former name | v0.4 name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `physics.scattering.interaction_constant(energy, units="rad/VA")` | `scatterem.physics.constants.phase_per_potential_at(kinetic_ev)` | rad/(V Å) |
| `physics.scattering.interaction_constant(energy, units="rad/A")` | `gamma_wavelength(kinetic_ev)` | `gamma * lambda` [Å] |
| `physics.scattering.electron_scattering_factor(z, gsq, units="VA")` | `POTENTIAL_PER_AMPLITUDE * born_amplitude(frequency, atomic_number)` | the argument is the frequency `g`, not `g**2`; the argument order changes; `born_amplitude` returns Å; the sum runs in float64 |
| `physics.scattering.electron_scattering_factor(z, gsq, units="A")` | `born_amplitude(frequency, atomic_number)` | as above |
| `physics.scattering.electron_scattering_factor_numpy(z, gsq, units)` | `born_amplitude_array(frequency, atomic_number)` | as above, numpy |
| `physics.scattering._electron_scattering_factors_numpy(zs, gsq, units)` | `born_amplitudes(frequency, atomic_numbers)` | as above, several elements |
| `physics.scattering.scattering_factors_on_grid(shape, extent, elements)` | `potential_spectra(grid, atomic_numbers)` | float64, not float32 [V Å³] |
| `physics.scattering._ANGSTROM_TO_VOLT_ANGSTROM` | `POTENTIAL_PER_AMPLITUDE` | |
| `physics.scattering._A`, `_B` | `scatterem.physics._lobato2014_table.COEFFICIENTS` | row `Z - 1` holds `(a_i, b_i)` |
| `physics.scattering._check_element(z)` | `validated_atomic_number(atomic_number)` | |

### The structure container (`scatterem.physics.atom_set`)

| Former name | v0.4 name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `Structure(unitcell, atoms, dwf, occ=None, Title="", EPS=1e-2, u_aniso=None)` | `AtomSet(box_spec, fractional, element_z, *, site_fraction=None, msd=None, adp=None, remark="", tilt_sine=5e-3)` | the `(N, 6)` table is gone: give the positions, atomic numbers, occupancies and `<u^2>` as separate arrays; `AtomSet` is immutable; `tilt_sine` has the role of `EPS`, with the default 5e-3 (was 1e-2): a cell edge tilts by at most 0.3° from its box axis, so bonds change by at most 0.5 %. Pass `tilt_sine=1e-2` for the v0.3 supercell of a triclinic cell |
| `Structure.unitcell` | `AtomSet.sides` | (3,) side lengths [Å] |
| `Structure.atoms[:, 0:3]` | `AtomSet.fractional` | |
| `Structure.atoms[:, 3]` | `AtomSet.element_z` | int64 |
| `Structure.atoms[:, 4]` | `AtomSet.site_fraction` | |
| `Structure.atoms[:, 5]` | `AtomSet.msd` | `<u^2>` [Å²] |
| `Structure.u_aniso` | `AtomSet.adp` | |
| `Structure.Title` | `AtomSet.remark` | |
| `Structure.fractional_occupancy` | `has_partial_occupancy(atom_set.site_fraction)` | tolerance `FULL_OCCUPANCY_TOLERANCE = 1e-4` (was 1e-3) |
| — | `AtomSet.xyz_angstrom`, `.box_volume`, `.row_total`, `len()`, `.with_fractional()` | new |
| `Structure.fromfile(fnam, temperature_factor_units="ums", atomic_coordinates="fractional", EPS, T, format)` | `read_atom_set(source_file, *, file_style=None, displacement_kind=None, position_kind=None, tilt_sine=5e-3)` | `file_style` in `("kirkland", "poscar", "mustem", "cif", "extxyz")`; `displacement_kind` in `("mean_square", "rms_length", "b_factor")`; no `T=` option |
| `.xyz` files: raw numbers kept by default | `.xyz` files: Cartesian Å by default | `position_kind="relative"` keeps the numbers as written |
| `.p1` atom lines `x y z label occ u` | the same layout reads; `x y z occ u label` also reads | one site label before or after the numbers is skipped; the label no longer sets the species, the element line and the counts do |
| `Structure.rotate(theta, axis, origin=(0.5, 0.5, 0.5), wrap=True, margin=0.0, rebox=True)` | `AtomSet.with_rotation(*, axis_vec, turn_radians, fixed_point=None, as_crystal=False, padding=0.0, tilt_sine=5e-3)` | returns a new object; the rotation is active and right-handed: v0.3 turned the atoms by `-theta`, so pass `turn_radians=-theta` for the v0.3 result. With `wrap=False`, v0.3 fitted the box to the turned atoms; `with_rotation` keeps the turned input box with its vacuum. The EELS tilt operators still use the v0.3 tight box |
| `Structure.tile(x=1, y=1, z=1)` (in place) | `AtomSet.replicated((n0, n1, n2))` | returns a new object; the order of the copies changes |
| `physics.structure.DEFAULT_MEAN_SQUARE_DISPLACEMENT` | `scatterem.crystal.phase.DEFAULT_U2` | 0.01 Å² |
| `physics._structure_files.read_xyz`, `read_p1`, `read_xtl`, `read_cif`, `read_extxyz`, `FORMATS`, `READERS` | `scatterem.physics._atom_set_io.read_structure_arrays`, `FILE_STYLES`, `SUFFIX_STYLE` | private |
| `physics._cell.reduce_cell`, `supercell_atoms`, `orthorhombic_cell` | `scatterem.physics._orthobox.plan_orthobox(lattice, tilt_sine)` and `OrthoPlan.apply(fractional)`; `plan_axis_aligned` | private; the supercell has the smallest `abs(det P)` |

### Crystal phases (`scatterem.crystal.phase`)

`Phase` keeps a crystal in its own cell, which can be oblique. It uses the
per-site names and checks of `AtomSet`. The `(N, 6)` table and the `unitcell`
and `atoms` attributes are gone.

| Former name | v0.4 name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `Phase(unitcell, atoms, name="", point_group=None, u_aniso=None)` | `Phase(cell, fractional, element_z, *, site_fraction=None, msd=None, adp=None, name="", point_group=None)` | give the sites as separate arrays; `Phase` is immutable; `msd=None` gives `DEFAULT_U2` |
| `Phase.unitcell` | `Phase.cell` | (3, 3), the edge vectors as rows [Å] |
| `Phase.atoms[:, 0:3]` | `Phase.fractional` | fractions of the cell edges |
| `Phase.atoms[:, 3]` | `Phase.element_z` | int64 |
| `Phase.atoms[:, 4]` | `Phase.site_fraction` | |
| `Phase.atoms[:, 5]` | `Phase.msd` | `<u^2>` [Å²] |
| `Phase.u_aniso` | `Phase.adp` | Cartesian in the frame of the cell rows |
| `Phase.from_cif(path, *, u2_default=0.01, name="")` | `Phase.from_cif(path, *, msd_default=0.01, name="")` | |
| — | `Phase.from_atom_set(structure, *, name=None)`, `.row_total`, `len()` | new. The same crystal in a rectangular box is `AtomSet(phase.cell, phase.fractional, phase.element_z, site_fraction=phase.site_fraction, msd=phase.msd, adp=phase.adp)` |

| Former name | v0.4 name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `make_potential(structure, pixels, subslices=None, tiling=(1, 1), ...)` | `potential_stack(partition, atom_set, points, *, replicas=None, ...)` | see the argument table below |
| `uniform_subslices(n)` | `BeamPartition.uniform(count)` | exact fractional edges |
| a list of slice ends `subslices` | `BeamPartition([0, *subslices])` or `BeamPartition.from_thicknesses(thicknesses, depth)` | |
| `subslice_bin_edges(subslices, edge_tol)` | `BeamPartition.edge_values(dtype, device)` | |
| `subslice_index_wrapped(z, subslices, edge_tol)` | `BeamPartition.bin_index(beam_fraction, *, edge_snap=True)` | |
| `subslice_index_clipped(z, subslices, edge_tol)` | `BeamPartition.bin_index_clamped(beam_fraction, *, edge_snap=True)` | |
| `element_order(structure)` | `species_order(atom_set)` | `scatterem.physics.beam_partition` |
| `share_splat()` | `spectrum_sweep(max_entries=4)` | `scatterem.physics.spectrum_sweep`; reuses the layout spectra between builds; `SweepLedger` counts the reuse |
| `_potential_deposition.replica_displacements(...)` | `jitter_offsets(atom_set, replicas, jitter, *, overrides=None, device=None)` | `scatterem.physics.thermal_jitter` |
| `_potential_deposition.representative_sites(table)` | `colocated_rows(source, sides=None, *, tolerance=0.01)` | `scatterem.physics.thermal_jitter` |
| `_potential_deposition.DepthModel`, `depth_model(...)` | `axial_shares(partition, beam_fraction, msd, depth, *, beam_spread="binned", edge_snap=True)` and `AxialShares` | `scatterem.physics.axial_shares` |
| `_potential_deposition.deposit(...)` | removed | private cubic B-spline deposit inside `potential_stack` |
| `_potential_common.validate_potential_inputs(...)` | `check_stack_request(...)` and `StackRequest` | `scatterem.physics.potential_stack` |
| `_potential_common.potential_device(device)` | `resolve_stack_device(...)` | |
| `_potential_common.POTENTIAL_BUILDERS = ("fft", "realspace")` | `ROUTE_NAMES = ("spectral", "spatial")` | `scatterem.physics.route_settings` |
| `_potential_common.resolve_potential_builder(request, decomposed=False)` | `choose_route(*, multi_device, preference="either")` | `"auto"` is now `"either"` |
| `_potential_common.check_potential_builder(builder)` | `check_route(value)` | |
| `_potential_common.resolve_bandwidth_limit(builder, value)`, `BANDWIDTH_AUTO`, `FFT_BANDWIDTH_DEFAULT = 0.2` | `route_rolloff(*, route, preference="either")`, `DEFAULT_ROLLOFF = 1/3` | the erf edge is now a Hann rolloff |
| `_potential_common.validate_taper_width(value, name)` | `check_rolloff(rolloff_depth)` | `scatterem.physics.potential_rolloff` |
| `_potential_common.validate_cutoff_tol(...)` | `check_cutoff(cutoff_level, *, field_label)` | |
| `RealspaceSpec(cutoff_tol=1e-3, projection="infinite", cutoff_tol_3d=None)` | `SpatialRouteSettings(axial_mode="projected", volume_cutoff=None, projected_cutoff=5e-4)` | `"finite"` is now `"sectioned"`; the default cutoff is 5e-4 V Å (was 1e-3): the radii grow by about 6 % and the truncation error halves. Pass `projected_cutoff=1e-3` for the v0.3 cut. |
| `_potential_common.SiteOverrides`, `resolve_site_overrides(...)` | `RowReplacements(beam_fraction=None, plane_fraction=None, msd=None, site_fraction=None)` | `scatterem.physics.row_replacements` |
| `_potential_common.uses_occupancy(...)` | `has_partial_occupancy(site_fraction)` and `ignore_site_fraction` | |
| `make_transmission_functions(potential, energy, *, bandwidth_limit=2/3, fftout=False, V_abs=None, dz=None)` | `thin_slice_transmission(beam_ev, projected, *, attenuation=None, bandlimit=None)` | `scatterem.physics.thin_slice`; no default band limit: give the fraction each time; no spectrum output (apply `torch.fft.fft2`); `attenuation` is the projected absorptive potential [V Å], not `V_abs` with `dz` |
| `projected_potential_to_object(potential, energy)` | `phase_from_projection(beam_ev, projected)` | |

Arguments of `make_potential` and their `potential_stack` replacement:

| `make_potential` | `potential_stack` | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `structure` | `atom_set` | second argument |
| `pixels` | `points` | third argument; integers only |
| `subslices=None` | `partition` | first argument, required |
| `tiling=(1, 1)` | `replicas=None` | `None` is one copy |
| `displacements=True`, `seed=None` | `jitter=None` or `jitter=ThermalJitter(draw_seed=seed)` | the default is now the static potential |
| `thermal_depth=False` | `ThermalJitter(transverse_only=True)` | `transverse_only=False` also moves the atoms along the beam |
| `fractional_occupancy=True` | `ignore_site_fraction=False` | inverted meaning |
| `sinc_deconvolution=True` | removed | the deposit is always corrected |
| `bandwidthlimit=0.2` | `rolloff=DEFAULT_ROLLOFF` (1/3) | a Hann rolloff; `None` turns it off |
| `fe=None` | `form_spectra=None` | |
| `weights=None`, `weight_power=1` | `atom_scale=None`, `scale_squared=False` | `scale_squared=True` for power 2 |
| `subslice_edge_tol=False` | `edge_snap=True` | the default changes: with `edge_snap=True`, a layer less than 1e-9 of the cell (float64; 512 ulp in float32) before an inner edge goes to the slice after it; a layer exactly on a float edge is always in the slice after it, as in v0.3 |
| `positions`, `depths`, `occupancy`, `u2` | `overrides=RowReplacements(plane_fraction=positions, beam_fraction=depths, site_fraction=occupancy, msd=u2)` | pass the four fields by keyword; the positional order is `beam_fraction, plane_fraction, msd, site_fraction` |
| `depth_split="nearest"` | `beam_spread="binned"` | `"tent"` and `"smeared"` are the other models |
| `dtype=torch.float32` | `dtype=None` | `None` is the torch default dtype; a complex dtype selects its real partner |
| `device=None` | `device=None` | |

The pixel value is now the band-limited point value of the projected
potential, not the pixel average. The atoms are put on the grid with a cubic
B-spline and two interlaced grids, not with bilinear weights.

### Constants, lens wavefront and masks

`scatterem.physics.constants`, `scatterem.physics.optics` and the Warp
device functions in `scatterem.physics.kernels.lens_wavefront_wp` are also
new code with a new API, written by the same two-team process. A constant
name now tells where its value comes from: `EXACT_` is a defining constant
of the SI, `CODATA18_` a CODATA 2018 value, `DERIVED_` a value that the
module computes from the others.

| Former name | v0.4 name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `PLANCK_CONSTANT` | `EXACT_PLANCK` | |
| `ELEMENTARY_CHARGE` | `EXACT_E_CHARGE` | |
| `SPEED_OF_LIGHT` | `EXACT_LIGHT_SPEED` | |
| `AVOGADRO_CONSTANT` | `EXACT_AVOGADRO` | |
| `BOLTZMANN_CONSTANT` | `EXACT_BOLTZMANN` | |
| `ELECTRON_REST_MASS` | `CODATA18_ELECTRON_MASS` | |
| `ATOMIC_MASS_CONSTANT` | `CODATA18_DALTON` | |
| `FINE_STRUCTURE_CONSTANT` | `CODATA18_FINE_STRUCTURE` | |
| `VACUUM_PERMEABILITY` | `CODATA18_VACUUM_MU` | |
| `CLASSICAL_ELECTRON_RADIUS` | `CODATA18_ELECTRON_RADIUS` | |
| `REDUCED_PLANCK_CONSTANT` | `DERIVED_PLANCK_BAR` | |
| `REST_ENERGY_EV` | `DERIVED_ELECTRON_REST_EV` | |
| `electron_wavelength(accelerating_voltage)` | `debroglie_at(kinetic_ev)` | |
| `relativistic_mass_factor(energy)` | `gamma_at(kinetic_ev)` | |
| `relativistic_electron_mass(energy)` | `moving_mass_at(kinetic_ev)` | |
| — | `DERIVED_AB_COUPLING` | new: the coupling `e / hbar` [rad / (T Å²)], a constant |
| — | `bend_per_tesla_at(kinetic_ev)` | new: `e / p` [1 / (T Å)]; refuses invalid energies, as the other functions do |
| `interaction_parameter(energy)` | `phase_per_potential_at(kinetic_ev)` | `scatterem.physics.atom_amplitudes` no longer re-exports it |
| `COEFFICIENT_NAMES` (`"C10"`, `"C12a"`, ...) | `LENS_LAYOUT` (`"C10"`, `"C12a"`, ...) | the same 12 labels in the same order; `scatterem.data.aberrations.CARTESIAN_NAMES` is the same tuple; `LENS_TERMS` gives `(n, m, part)` of each slot |
| `cartesian_chi(qy, qx, wavelength, coefficients)` | `lens_wavefront(lens, fy, fx, *, lambda_a)` | the lens vector comes first; `lambda_a` is a host number, not a tensor |
| `cartesian_chi_gradient(qy, qx, wavelength, coefficients)` | `lens_wavefront_slope(lens, fy, fx, *, lambda_a)` | the result is `(..., 2)` with `[..., 0] = dW/dk_y`, not `(2, ...)`; use `.unbind(-1)` |
| `polar_to_cartesian(dict)` | `lens_from_amplitude(tensor)` | a `(..., 12)` tensor in `AMPLITUDE_LAYOUT` (magnitude slots `"C12"`, `"C21"`, ..., angle slots `"phi12"`, `"phi21"`, ...); `pack_lens(mapping, layout=AMPLITUDE_LAYOUT)` builds it from labels |
| `cartesian_to_polar(dict)` | `lens_to_amplitude(tensor)` | `unpack_lens(..., layout=AMPLITUDE_LAYOUT)` gives a dict; the angle is in `[0, 2 pi / m)`, not `(-pi / m, pi / m]` |
| `APERTURE_EDGE_PX` (1.0) | `RIM_WIDTH_PX` (2.0) | the default rim is 2 pixels |
| `circular_aperture(r, shape, aa_width=1.0, device=None, aspect=1.0)` | `smooth_disc(shape, radius_px, *, rim_px=RIM_WIDTH_PX, px_ratio=None, dtype=None, device=None)` | pass `rim_px=1.0` for the v0.3 rim |
| `annular_aperture(r_inner, r_outer, shape, device=None)` | `smooth_annulus(shape, inner_px, outer_px, *, rim_px=RIM_WIDTH_PX, px_ratio=None, dtype=None, device=None)` | pass `rim_px=1.0` for the v0.3 rim |
| — | `illumination_disc(shape, step_inv_a, opening_rad, *, lambda_a, dtype=None, device=None)` | new: the disc of a convergent beam; the rim is always `RIM_WIDTH_PX`; for a 1-pixel rim use `smooth_disc(shape, opening_rad / (lambda_a * dk_y), rim_px=1.0, px_ratio=dk_x / dk_y)` |
| `kernels.aberrations.aberration_function_cartesian(qy, qx, wavelength, aberrations)` | `kernels.lens_wavefront_wp.lens_wavefront_f32(lens, fy, fx, lambda_a)` | new argument order |
| `kernels.aberrations.aberration_function_cartesian_defocus_only(...)` | `kernels.lens_wavefront_wp.lens_wavefront_focus_f32(lens, fy, fx, lambda_a)` | the same bits as `lens_wavefront_f32` when slots 1 to 11 are zero |
| — | `kernels.lens_wavefront_wp.lens_to_warp(lens, *, device=None)` | new: a lens vector as a float32 Warp array |

Behaviour that changes:

- The masks are in DFT order on every axis. On an axis of odd length the v0.3
  masks were not (`fftshift(arange(-n // 2, n // 2))`), so values on odd axes
  change. On even axes the masks are the same to float32 rounding. The masks
  use the torch default dtype and device; v0.3 gave float32 on the CPU.
- The functions of `scatterem.physics.constants` refuse zero (except
  `gamma_at` and `moving_mass_at`), negative, NaN and infinite energies with
  `ValueError`, and a `bool` with `TypeError`. v0.3 returned a number, NaN or
  raised `ZeroDivisionError`.
- `lens_wavefront` has a finite gradient at `k = 0`; v0.3 gave NaN there.
  A lens tensor must be on the device of the frequency grid; the result has
  the dtype of the grid.
- Numbers: the constants are the same values. The wavelength and the
  interaction parameter agree with v0.3 to 4.5e-16 (relative), the wavefront
  and its slope to 7.5e-16 (float64) and 3.7e-7 (float32), and the Warp
  wavefront to 1.3e-7 (float32).
- The PRISM and PRISM-EELS probes and beam sets keep the 1-pixel rim of
  v0.3, so the beam sets are the same.
- The probe apertures of the simulation and of the PRISM models are computed
  in float64 and then cast. On 60 random windows they differ from v0.3 by at
  most about 3e-6, with the same beam support. The v0.3 float32 aperture
  rounded the radius and the distance to float32 before the edge function,
  so the v0.4 values are the more accurate ones. Exception: on an axis of odd
  length, where the disc reaches the highest frequency, v0.3 had the wrong
  frequency order (see the first item of this list).
- The direct-ptychography log gives the astigmatism and coma angles in
  `[0, 2 pi / m)`, not in `(-pi / m, pi / m]`. The fit does not change.
- v0.4 has one set of aberration labels: the Krivanek names (`"C10"`,
  `"C12a"`, ...). `LENS_LAYOUT` and
  `scatterem.data.aberrations.CARTESIAN_NAMES` are the same tuple. The
  `Aberrations` container, `pack_lens`, `unpack_lens` and the
  direct-ptychography configuration use these labels.
- v0.4 has one polar form. `scatterem.data.aberrations.POLAR_NAMES` and
  `AMPLITUDE_LAYOUT` are the same tuple: the seven magnitudes (`"C10"`,
  `"C12"`, ..., `"C34"`), then the five angles (`"phi12"`, ...,
  `"phi34"`). `Aberrations.to_polar`, `to_polar_array`, `from_polar` and
  `from_polar_array` use `lens_to_amplitude` and `lens_from_amplitude`.
  `to_polar` and `to_polar_array` now give each angle in `[0, 2 pi / m)`,
  not in `(-pi / m, pi / m]`. The magnitudes and the lens do not change.

| `vis.calibration._plot_com(...)` | `vis.rotation_figures.plot_scan_maps(scan_images, *, scan_spacing, distance_unit, ...)` | |
| `reconstruction.ptychography.direct.bright_field_shifts(G_ref, vBF, ..., bin, n_batches=16, registration_upsample_factor=10, verbosity=1, fwhm_lowpass_bf=None, peak_selection="argmax")` | `reconstruction.ptychography.direct.measure_bf_parallax(image_spectra, detector_coords_px, *, shift_estimator="mean_template", binning=1, peak_grid_divisor=20, lowpass_sigma_px=None, start_template=None, n_refinements=2, peak_tolerance=0.02, remove_image_mean=True, status_line=False, quiet=False)` | the spectra come as a stack or a `SpectrumSource`; the low-pass width is a standard deviation, not a FWHM |
| `reconstruction.ptychography.direct.bright_field_shifts_pairwise(..., connectivity=8)` | `measure_bf_parallax(..., shift_estimator="neighbour_mesh")` | |

### Bright-field disk and Fourier grids

v0.4 replaces the bright-field disk fit (`scatterem.data.disk_fit`) and the
frequency grid and ring profile (`scatterem.utils.grids`) with new code that
has a new API: `scatterem.data.pupil_gauge` and
`scatterem.utils.spectral_mesh`. Two teams wrote it, as for the physics base
layer. The numbers change:

- The disk radius is now the radius of the circle at the level halfway
  between the inside and the outside intensity. v0.3 took the median radius
  of a threshold sweep that was a fraction of the maximum, so a dark offset
  moved it. On synthetic disks the radius error goes from 1.2 % to 0.14 %
  (radius 8 px), from 2.7 % to 0.01 % with a 20 % dark offset, and from 14 %
  to 0.9 % (rms) at 10 counts per pixel. `dk = alpha / (lambda R)` changes
  with it.
- `measure_pupil` and the `Dataset4DStem` methods
  `bright_field_radius_and_center`, `bright_field_radius_and_center_` and
  `calibrate_reciprocal_from_bright_field` take `edge_reach=None` by
  default: an edge band of 2 pixels for `"integral"` and 10 pixels for
  `"rayfit"`. With 2 pixels, `"rayfit"` reads a disk with a 90-degree notch
  about 11 % small, so it keeps the wide band. On a disk whose top
  falls towards the edge, a wide band reads the radius too small: on the
  Gd2O3 data of the FF-STEM paper, 4.1 % inside the half-level crossing of
  the azimuthal profile with 10 pixels and 0.5 % with 2 pixels. On the four
  FF-STEM datasets, `dk` from `calibrate_reciprocal_from_bright_field` then
  differs from v0.3 by -0.36 % (carbon), +0.01 % (Co3O4), -0.003 % (Gd2O3)
  and -0.03 % (Au).
- The ring profile uses the coarsest axis step as the shell spacing and keeps
  only complete shells, so it has fewer values than in v0.3 (64 x 64: 31, not
  33; 64 x 40: 19, not 33). The error against an analytic Gaussian profile
  drops by a factor of 1.3 to 6.
- `dual_mesh` rounds each frequency once from its exact value. v0.3 values
  can differ by 1 ulp.

| Former name | v0.4 name | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `utils.grids.fft_frequencies_2d(shape, sampling=(1.0, 1.0), half_pixel_shift=False, device="cpu", dtype=None)` | `utils.spectral_mesh.dual_mesh(n_yx, pitch, *, staggered, dtype=None, device=None)` | `pitch` and `staggered` have no default; give `staggered=False` for the standard grid; zero, negative or non-finite pitches and counts raise |
| `utils.grids.frequency_magnitude_2d(shape, sampling, device, dtype)` | removed | `torch.hypot(*dual_mesh(...))` |
| `utils.grids.grid_shape_and_sampling(q)` | removed | keep the shape and the pitch with the grid |
| `utils.grids.radial_average(image, sampling)` | `utils.spectral_mesh.shell_means(spectrum_samples, pitch)` | returns `ShellMeans(shell_wavenumber, shell_average)`; a complex input raises `TypeError` (pass `.real` or `abs()`); code that indexes by the v0.3 length or spacing must change |
| `utils.data.disk_fit.fit_bright_field_disk(dp, *, threshold_range=(0.25, 0.75), n_thresholds=100, max_radius_fraction=0.4, min_contrast=3.0)` | `data.pupil_gauge.measure_pupil(pupil_frame, estimator="integral", *, radius_cap=0.45, contrast_floor=1.5, edge_reach=None, arc_floor=None)` | returns `PupilEstimate(rim_radius, rim_center)`; tuple unpacking `radius, center = ...` still works |
| `method="area"` (development code only) | `estimator="integral"` | needs a complete disk; a disk cut by the detector border raises `ValueError` |
| `method="circle"` (development code only) | `estimator="rayfit"` | for a notched disk or a disk partly outside the detector; it uses no random numbers |
| `max_radius_fraction=0.4` | `radius_cap=0.45` | the default accepts slightly larger disks |
| `min_contrast=3.0` | `contrast_floor=1.5` | the smallest inside/outside level ratio; set it to refuse weak disks as before |
| `min_edge_points` (a number of points; development code only) | `arc_floor` (a fraction of the full circle, `"rayfit"` only) | default 0.4 |
| `threshold_range`, `n_thresholds`, `edge_method`, `ransac_iterations`, `ransac_threshold` | removed | `edge_reach` sets the width of the edge band; increase it for very soft edges |
| — | `edge_reach=None` (`measure_pupil` and the `Dataset4DStem` disk methods) | new default: a band of 2 pixels for `estimator="integral"` and 10 pixels for `estimator="rayfit"`; pass a number to set the band for both |
| `Dataset4dstem.bright_field_radius_and_center(thresh_lower=0.1, thresh_upper=0.6, N=100, method="area", edge_method="canny", min_edge_points=100, ransac_iterations=1000, ransac_threshold=2.0)` | `Dataset4DStem.bright_field_radius_and_center(estimator="integral", *, edge_reach=None, arc_floor=None)` | returns a `PupilEstimate`; the same change for `bright_field_radius_and_center_`; the default `edge_reach=None` is the default of `measure_pupil` (see the next row) |
| `Dataset4dstem.crop_brightfield_(thresh_lower=0.01, thresh_upper=0.99, normalize=True, clip_neg_values=True)` | `Dataset4DStem.crop_brightfield_(estimator="integral", normalize=True, clip_neg_values=True)` | |
| `Dataset4dstem.calibrate_reciprocal_from_bright_field(semiconvergence_angle=None, thresh_lower=0.1, thresh_upper=0.99, method="area")` | `Dataset4DStem.calibrate_reciprocal_from_bright_field(semiconvergence_angle=None, estimator="integral", *, edge_reach=None)` | the radius comes from the whole detector, not from the bright-field crop |

## Other behaviour changes

- `import scatterem` no longer sets `torch.set_float32_matmul_precision("medium")`.
  The precision stays at the torch default, `"highest"`. The published FF-STEM
  figures were computed at `"medium"`. On the four figure scripts the change is
  of the order of the run-to-run difference (at most 4e-7 relative L2 on carbon,
  Co₃O₄ and Au, 2e-4 on Gd₂O₃), and setting `"medium"` does not give
  the published figures back. See [Figure scripts](figures.qmd). The complex64
  PRISM-EELS calls run up to 1.5x slower than in v0.3 at `"highest"`. Call
  `scatterem.configure(matmul_precision="medium")` to get the v0.3 speed; see
  [the cost of a call](eels.qmd#the-cost-of-a-call-v03-and-v04).
- The aberration autofocus uses the exact derivative of its objective and
  ignores the scan DC of each bright-field pixel. Fitted aberrations change; on
  the Gd₂O₃ figure data C10 moves from 31.5 Å to 19.6 Å.
- `import scatterem` still initialises Warp: it imports
  `scatterem.reconstruction`, which calls `warp.init()`. `scatterem.nn` does
  the same. The lower layers (`scatterem.physics`, `scatterem.data`) start Warp
  only at their first Warp call.
- The tilt-corrected dark field and the fusion shift each detector segment by
  its full parallax. v0.3 divided the shift by $2\pi$ a second time. Results
  change when C10 or A1 is not zero.
- Direct ptychography defaults to `phase_sign="preserve"` (positive phase for
  positive potential). v0.3 flipped each image to positive skewness, which is
  `phase_sign="positive"`. `FusedFullFieldConfig` has the same `phase_sign`
  field for its ptychography channel.
- The bright-field mask threshold is a fraction of a robust reference level, so
  a few hot pixels no longer set it. Without hot pixels the mask is the same.
- `reconstruction_sampling` no longer takes `units=`.
- `interaction_constant` is now `scatterem.physics.constants.phase_per_potential_at(kinetic_ev)`.
- v0.4 keeps no compatibility aliases. These alias names are removed:
  `PrismScanOp.f` (use `fy` and `fx`), `SMeta.q_dft` (use `qf`),
  `RadialWavefunction` (use `scatterem.simulation.eels.AtomicRadialWavefunction`,
  the same class) and the module
  `scatterem.utils.energy` (use `scatterem.physics.constants.debroglie_at`;
  an angular pixel in mrad is `1e3 * debroglie_at(energy) * dq`).
- `Dataset4dstemOutOfCore` is removed. Use
  `Dataset4DStem.from_array(..., out_of_core=True)`.
- Five helper modules are internal in v0.4 and not part of the public API:
  `scatterem.data.storage`, `scatterem.utils.env`,
  `scatterem.utils.lazy_plotting`, `scatterem.utils.warp` and
  `scatterem.nn.functional.warp.prism_project._basis` (was
  `prism_project.basis`). The package uses them, so they ship, but the API
  reference does not list them and their names can change without notice.
  The `scatterem.utils.warp` names in the table below are internal for the
  same reason.
- New required dependencies: `cmcrameri>=1.10` and `imageio>=2.33`. New
  optional extras: `triton`, `notebook` and `anim` (`imageio-ffmpeg`, for MP4
  output of the animations). The `dev` extra adds `mpmath`. The `eels` extra
  (`gpaw`, `ase`) is unchanged.
- Higher dependency floors: `numpy>=2.1`, `scipy>=1.15`, `matplotlib>=3.10`
  (was 3.7), `h5py>=3.12.1`, `scikit-image>=0.25` and `gdown>=4.7.3` (was
  4.7.0). These are the first releases with wheels for CPython
  3.10 to 3.13. Python 3.10 or newer is still required, as in v0.3.

longer part of the public interface. The last rows list the names that v0.3
exported from its private (underscore) modules. A check imports each v0.4 path
in this table against the released tree.
